analysis.title: Global Economic Weekly: After the Blue Tsunami (6 November 2026)
key_insights: BofA reads the US midterm result as a Democratic sweep larger than a Blue Wave. It lists likely effects: headwinds to the AI buildout, lower odds of Iran escalation, more protracted debt limit talks, higher spending and deficits with higher taxes later, and a stronger mandate and independence for the Fed.

Democrats won in most states where data center buildout is concentrated, so more local data center regulation is likely. BofA says this could slow the AI trade and capex cycle, which it calls two pillars of recent US growth, and ties it to the equity selloff since the election.

Since the election the S&P 500 is down 2.8%, Nasdaq down 5.5% and the semiconductor index down 14%. This accelerates a trend that began before the election as a Democratic sweep became more likely and funding and monetization worries about AI grew.

BofA US economics argues regulation will raise data center costs but will not stop the investment cycle. Regulation is expected to centre on shielding consumers from utility costs and tougher environmental standards. Capex booms end when demand growth stops outpacing supply growth. Regulation is not expected to affect the roughly 70GW of power under construction, and AI investment is still expected to add 30-50bp to growth next year.

BofA equity strategy estimates AI-related revenue growth will exceed capex growth as early as 3Q 2027, which would justify about 350GW of planned or under-construction capacity. Hyperscaler 2027 capex expectations were revised higher again, so BofA sees demand and monetization as the real risk, with regulation acting as a speed bump that could also shrink the size of an eventual bust.

BofA says a slower AI buildout has a silver lining. It could lower the risk of a sharper contraction later, limit recession risk and put less pressure on the Fed to hike. It also flags that tighter US regulation could marginally benefit China and could divert data center construction to Canada, the Nordics, India, Mexico or Brazil.

Oil fell after the election as markets priced a higher chance of a US-Iran deal. BofA thinks the fall may be unwarranted because a resolution still looks elusive. A ceasefire could push oil and gas toward surplus and take Brent to $80/bbl or lower on average next year.

BofA expects deficits around 6% of GDP and an unsustainable debt trajectory to keep real interest rates high absent an AI-trade breakdown or an economic slowdown. It sees higher taxes, mainly on high earners, as the path of least resistance and a VAT as the efficient option that politics will likely skip.

Democratic control of the Senate makes future Trump nominees to the Fed Board easy to block, which should support Fed independence. BofA says the affordability focus may argue for a stronger price-stability mandate and a more hawkish reaction function. Its base case stays at two more Fed hikes, in December and March.
The size of the Blue Sweep limits the risk of a major trade policy escalation in 2027. Texas is now the key Republican swing state, which could strengthen Canada and Mexico in USMCA renegotiations.

Riksbank hiked 25bp to 2% as expected and kept its September rate path. BofA expects one more 25bp hike in 1Q27, most likely February, with a terminal rate of 2.25%, and sees a short cycle that is less hawkish than the market. Norges Bank held at 4.5% with a tightening bias, and BofA thinks the rate has likely peaked.

The Riksbank plans to borrow about SEK200bn to fund FX reserves, about SEK100bn of which could go into spot SEK purchases from 2027 over 12-18 months. BofA sees modest upside risk to SEK, though the 2023 precedent suggests a smaller impact because SEK positioning was shorter then. NOK faces downside from lower energy prices and geopolitics.

BoE hiked 25bp to 4.25% territory expectations, described by BofA as a hawkish hike: the vote was 8-1 with one vote for 50bp, inflation is projected to peak at 4.9% in Q2 2027, and Lombardelli and Pill opened the door to near-term action. Bailey pushed back on pricing of four hikes, and BofA still sees that pricing as excessive. It expects a second hike in February, but December risk has risen.

Rengo set FY27 Shunto targets of about 6% headline and about 4% base pay, up from 5% or more and 3% or more. BofA still expects base-pay hikes near the recent 3.5% pace with upside risk. A move toward 4% would reinforce its call for three more BoJ hikes (December 2026, March 2027, July 2027) and raise the risk of a terminal rate above 2%.

BofA expects CEMAC to clear regional financing assurances by year-end, with Gabon reaching a staff-level agreement with the IMF by Q1 2027 and Congo in Q4 2026. It does not expect an IMF programme for Cameroon for now. Local debt markets are near saturation, with Gabon paying all-in yields of 12-15%.

BofA puts the effective fiscal cost of Lula's R$405bn promise package at R$157bn for committed measures (R$92bn in 2026, R$65bn in 2027). The headline counts credit envelopes, not direct cost. Part of the deterioration is permanent, and a primary surplus of about 3.0% of GDP would be needed to stabilize gross debt.
earnings_insights: Hyperscalers were penalized for any softness in results, per BofA equity strategy, yet they have shown no sign of cutting capex and 2027 capex expectations were revised higher again.

Hyperscaler AI-related revenue growth (MSFT Azure and other cloud, AMZN AWS, GOOGL Google Cloud, META advertising, ORCL cloud) continues to climb through 3Q26 per Visible Alpha data cited in the report.

risk_factors: Local data center regulation in Texas, Ohio and Georgia, which hold 35% of under-construction capacity, could slow the AI buildout and weigh on the AI trade.
AI monetization and demand: capex booms end when demand growth stops outpacing supply growth, and hyperscalers are penalized for softness in results.
Protracted 2027 debt limit negotiations and a structural deficit near 6% of GDP that keeps real interest rates high.
A US-Iran resolution that fails to arrive, or energy prices rising sharply again, would raise inflation and second-round effects (BoE adverse scenario peaks at 6.2% in Q3 2027).
Energy-price and geopolitical downside for NOK, and weaker external demand for Sweden.
Shunto base-pay settlements near 4% would raise BoJ overshoot concerns.
Brazil: permanent new spending raises the expenditure base beyond 2027 and the fiscal adjustment required.
charts_described: Exhibit 3: S&P 500 -2.8%, Nasdaq 100 -5.5% and S&P semiconductors -14.0% since election day, versus -1.2%, -3.7% and -8.5% from Sep 1 to election day.
Exhibit 4 (NBC News): importance of AI and data centers to a congressional vote was crucial for 23%, a major factor for 33%, a minor factor for 31% and not a factor for 13%.
Exhibit 8: Riksbank underlying CPIF excluding energy and temporary fiscal measures was 1.6% in September and is expected to rise above 2% next year.
Exhibit 12: BoE central projection has inflation peaking at 4.9%, with a weaker demand scenario at 4.8% and an adverse inflation scenario at 6.2% (Q3 2027).
Exhibit 14: Rengo base-pay realization ratio has risen to around 80%.
Exhibit 15: Brazil measures not pending legislative approval add up to R$92bn in 2026 and R$65bn in 2027.
vol_and_positioning: SEK positioning was considerably shorter during the 2023 Riksbank hedging programme than BofA assumes now, so the impact of the new reserve-financing operation could be smaller this time.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict: the midterm result raised market odds of a deal or lower escalation risk and oil fell, but BofA says a resolution still looks elusive.

US AI leadership: tighter US regulation of AI and data centers could marginally benefit China, though US policymakers may limit the damage and aligned countries such as Canada or the Nordics could gain data center investment.
US trade policy and USMCA: the Blue Sweep limits scope for trade escalation, and Texas as the key swing state could strengthen Canada and Mexico in renegotiation.
Central Africa: CEMAC governments (Gabon, Congo, Cameroon) are working toward IMF staff-level agreements and regional financing assurances, with extractive-sector FX repatriation talks on hold.
Brazil: Lula's re-election promises and the next Finance Minister's mandate are key for the fiscal outlook.

tension_points.theme: AI capex versus data center regulation
tension_points.bull_case: Regulation is likely to be consumer-protection and environmental rules that raise costs but do not cancel projects. Demand supports capex: hyperscaler AI-related revenue growth keeps climbing, 2027 capex expectations were revised higher, and AI revenue growth is estimated to exceed capex growth by 3Q 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Voter opposition to data centers has picked up, 40 of 41 ballot measures passed, and Democratic wins in Texas, Ohio and Georgia put 35% of under-construction capacity under possible tighter rules. The equity market has already sold off, with semiconductors down 14%, on monetization and funding concerns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Demand growth no longer outpacing supply growth, or monetization failing (including AI cannibalizing existing revenue), would break the bull case.

tension_points.theme: BoE hiking path versus market pricing
tension_points.bull_case: A hawkish hike with an 8-1 vote, a 4.9% projected inflation peak and Lombardelli and Pill pointing to near-term action make a December hike live.
tension_points.bear_case: Bailey said the hike is not the start of an inevitable sequence, some of the curve is risk premium, medium-term inflation of 1.8% implicitly pushes back on four hikes, and BofA sees limited evidence of second-round effects.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Higher energy prices or upside data surprises (two inflation and labour prints plus 2027 pay settlements before December) would make a December hike likely, while a US-Iran resolution or lower energy futures would favour a February second hike only.

tension_points.bull_case: A stronger Fed mandate and independence, with blockable nominees and an affordability focus, could support a more hawkish reaction function with more proactive tightening.
tension_points.bear_case: A slower AI cycle could bring cooler growth, inflation and interest rates, reducing pressure on the Fed to hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A breakdown in the AI trade or another shock triggering an economic slowdown would remove the case for sustained high real rates.

theme_stances.key_argument: Regulation raises costs but does not stop the investment cycle because demand and monetization decide whether capex busts.
theme_stances.evidence: the growth impulse from AI investment should remain intact

theme_stances.key_argument: Four total BoE hikes would require actual second-round effects, which are not yet visible.
theme_stances.evidence: we still continue to view market pricing of four total hikes as excessive

theme_stances.key_argument: Oil fell on higher deal odds, but a resolution of the Iran conflict still looks elusive.
